headline: Kotak Institutional Equities prefers mid-cap IT stocks over TCS and Infosys
hook: Mid-tier IT firms favored over industry giants

modes.bear: Large-cap IT stocks provide stability and dividend consistency that mid-tier firms may lack during market volatility.
modes.bull: Mid-tier firms have more room for margin expansion and growth compared to the saturated large-cap segment.
modes.simple: A major brokerage thinks smaller IT companies will grow faster than giants like TCS and Infosys, potentially shifting investor interest.

summary: Kotak Institutional Equities has shifted its preference toward mid-tier IT companies like Tech Mahindra, Persistent Systems, and Coforge. The brokerage suggests these firms offer better growth potential compared to industry leaders TCS and Infosys. This outlook is based on current market positioning and expected performance trajectories for the mid-cap segment. Retail investors holding large-cap IT stocks may see a shift in institutional interest toward these smaller challengers.
why_it_matters: Mid-cap IT stocks may outperform large-cap leaders in coming quarters.
winners_losers: Mid-tier IT firms gain / Large-cap IT firms hurt

headline: Persistent Systems standalone revenue rises 28.66% in September quarter
hook: Persistent Systems reports strong double-digit revenue growth
summary: Persistent Systems reported standalone net sales of Rs 4,494.17 crore for the quarter ended September 2026. This represents a 28.66% increase compared to the same period last year. The figures reflect the company's standalone financial performance for the quarter.
why_it_matters: Strong revenue growth signals robust demand for IT services.

headline: Persistent Systems to raise Rs 6,000 crore via NCDs
summary: Persistent Systems is raising over Rs 6,000 crore through non-convertible debentures to fund its $1.25 billion acquisition of Nagarro SE. The company recently completed a qualified institutional placement (QIP) that raised Rs 4,264 crore. Persistent has already secured 94% of Nagarro shares following a successful tender offer. The NCDs will have maturities ranging from one to five years.
whats_next: Finalization of debt financing and integration of Nagarro SE operations.
why_it_matters: Debt-funded acquisition increases leverage for the company.

headline: Persistent Systems raises Rs 4,264 crore via QIP, backed mostly by domestic mutual funds
hook: Domestic funds anchor mid-tier tech capital raise
summary: Persistent Systems has successfully raised Rs 4,264 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) of shares. The capital raise saw major participation from domestic mutual funds, who received the vast majority of shares representing 5% or more of the offering. Government Pension Fund Global stood out as the sole foreign portfolio investor to secure a significant allocation. Retail investors in IT stocks should note this strong domestic institutional backing for mid-tier tech expansion.
why_it_matters: Strong domestic fund backing signals institutional confidence in mid-cap IT growth.
winners_losers: Persistent Systems gains / existing shareholders diluted slightly

headline: Persistent Systems allots over 7.6 million securities through QIP
hook: Massive equity dilution via QIP allotment
summary: Persistent Systems Limited announced the allotment of 7,683,981 securities following a Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) approved at its board meeting on October 26, 2026. This capital-raising exercise increases the total equity base of the company. Existing retail shareholders face equity dilution as new institutional shares enter the market. For Indian retail investors, large QIPs alter the equity structure and can temporarily pressure stock prices before deploying capital for growth.
why_it_matters: Equity dilution impacts your existing share value.
winners_losers: Institutional investors gain / retail shareholders diluted

why_it_matters: Eligible shareholders will receive a substantial cash credit in their accounts.
